name: Executive order of March 18, 1879 making an addition to the White Earth Reservation
promises: This was an executive order, not a treaty. The President set apart land north of the White Earth Reservation of the treaty of March 19, 1867, running north from its northwest corner (T. 146 N., R. 42 W.) and east to the Red Lake reservation line, as an addition to White Earth.
landTaken: None by this order: it added land (Royce area 610).
today: Royce records that this tract, in two separate pieces, was restored to the public domain by executive order of July 13, 1883. That restoration is a separate event and is not counted here.

sources.title: Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule p. 894, executive order of March 18, 1879
Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule p. 895, remark and area 610

openQuestions: The July 13, 1883 restoration took this addition back; whether any court or Commission finding covers it was not researched. Under the rule for executive-order land, the restoration alone is not a breach.
The order was read only in Royce's summary. The treaty date Royce gives for White Earth (March 19, 1867) was not rechecked here.
No White Earth Nation account of this addition was located.

Audit 2026-11-08: Royce pp. 894-895 reopened: boundaries, area 610 (Minnesota 2) and the remark that the tract was restored by executive order of July 13, 1883 in two separate pieces confirmed. ICC full-text search on White Earth and 1879 found no finding about this addition.

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for Court of Claims "Chippewa" (opened 80 Ct. Cl. 410, 87 Ct. Cl. 1, 88 Ct. Cl. 1, 90 Ct. Cl. 140, 91 Ct. Cl. 97) and ICC full text "White Earth 1879 addition" (opened OSU 638); nothing new. 80 Ct. Cl. 410 (1935) mentions an executive order of March 18, 1879 withdrawing a tract bounded in part by the Red Lake reservation, only as background to the Red Lake title.
